what: color.py --keep-alpha --source-alpha-mode premultiplied on a BT.709-tagged ProRes 4444 master wrote the graded colour with the BT.601 matrix while the stream stayed tagged BT.709: the wide merge leg's `format=gbrp16le` converted the graded YUV to RGB with swscale's default, so an opaque pixel came out as a BT.709->BT.601 shift from the straight run's (the reporter read 181,129,75 where straight wrote 177,126,77 under a LUT; with --correct, 92.6,187.8,255 against 83.2,183.4,255). qtrle, whose line is RGB and takes the alphamerge leg, did not show it.
escaped: The #453 test grades a premultiplied fixture in ProRes 4444 and qtrle and compares each partial band's re-straightened colour with the same run's opaque band; a matrix shift moves every band alike, so the test passed while the whole premultiplied run was shifted against the straight run. The wide leg was the one conversion in the alpha path with no matrix named: everything before it is labelled or pinned by the grade's own legs, and finish_chain() names both matrix legs of its premultiply, so only a pixel readback of two runs, or the reporter's comparison, shows it.
mechanism: alpha.wide_merge_leg() is the one builder of that leg (color.py calls it for a premultiplied ProRes 4444 master) and converts the graded YUV to the RGB its premultiply needs with the matrix the samples are in: the source's matrix (BT.601 named where the source is tagged that), the BT.709 an RGB source on a YUV line is converted to (#496), and nothing invented for an untagged source, where swscale's own default stands. tests/test_delivery.py's test_color_source_alpha_mode_premultiplied_on_a_tagged_master_matches_straight_740 grades a BT.709-tagged premultiplied fixture with --correct --gamma and compares the opaque pixel with the straight run's (and pins the leg's matrix in the dry-run command); tests/test_contract.py's PremultipliedMergeMatrix740Tests pins the leg for a BT.709, a BT.601, an untagged and an RGB source and that color.py builds it through the helper. docs/design-decisions.md states the rule beside #453.
